name: MelonLoader mod
summary: A mod dll for MelonLoader, for Unity Mono and IL2CPP games. The usual choice for BONELAB, Schedule I and Phasmophobia.
description: A C# class library that MelonLoader loads from the game's Mods folder. Pick the game and the project references MelonLoader and the game's assemblies from the game folder and copies the built dll into Mods after every build.

options.label: Mod name
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only

options.label: Author
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only
options.help: Shown next to the mod's name in the MelonLoader console.

options.label: Game folder
options.help: The folder with the game's exe. Leave empty to add the game dlls by hand later.

options.label: Game type
options.help: Set from the game when a game is picked. A mod built for one type does not load in the other.

options.label: Target framework
options.help: Mono games only; IL2CPP mods are always net6.0. Set from the game's Unity version when a game is picked.

options.label: Unity version
options.help: Only used for a Mono game when no game folder is set: Unity's assemblies then come from NuGet.

options.label: MelonLoader package version
options.help: Only used while MelonLoader is not installed in the game folder: the project then compiles against the LavaGang.MelonLoader NuGet package.

options.label: Game developer
options.help: First line of <Game>_Data\app.info, copied exactly. Leave empty and the mod loads in any game.

options.label: Game name
options.help: Second line of <Game>_Data\app.info, copied exactly. A wrong value here stops the mod from loading.

options.label: Harmony patches
options.help: A Patches folder with an example of changing a game method.

options.label: Preferences
options.help: Settings saved to UserData\MelonPreferences.cfg that players can edit.

options.label: Hotkey
options.help: A key press handler in OnUpdate.

options.label: Copy the dll into the game's Mods folder after each build

next: Open the folder in Visual Studio, Rider or VS Code.
Install MelonLoader in the game and start the game once, then build: dotnet build -c Release
The dll is in bin\Release. With a game folder set it is also copied to the game's Mods folder.
Start the game and look for the mod's line in the MelonLoader console or in MelonLoader\Latest.log.
Your code starts in Core.cs, in OnInitializeMelon.
